channel.title: OurWord — 160 people and books on how the world actually works, across 2,600 years
channel.description: A knowledge base of the durable rules people have worked out about strategy, money, power, human nature and building things — drawn from 160 figures and classic texts across 2,600 years. Each entry gives the one idea that person is actually remembered for, the story behind it, the sub-principles with worked examples, and how it applies today.

item.title: Alfred Adler · Whose task is this
item.description: Alfred Adler · Whose task is this — Draw the line where the bill lands. Most of the pain in a relationship comes from crossing a line nobody drew. This is where the line actually runs.

item.title: Alfred Adler · Not because — in order to
item.description: Alfred Adler · Not because — in order to — Swap the cause for the purpose. Freud asks what happened to you. Adler asks what you are using it for. Why changing the question unfreezes things.

item.title: The Analects · Knowing what you know
item.description: The Analects · Knowing what you know — The half that has to be said out loud. Read as modesty it is a platitude. Read as an instruction it is an operation that very few people can actually perform.

item.title: The Analects · Three layers of looking at a person
item.description: The Analects · Three layers of looking at a person — Each layer is harder to fake than the last. Everyone misreads people. The useful part of his method is the order: the three layers get progressively harder to perform.

item.title: The Analects · Do not do it to them
item.description: The Analects · Do not do it to them — The one word he said would last a lifetime. Zigong asked for a single word to live by. The part worth noticing is that what came back was a prohibition.

item.title: The Analects · Harmony is not sameness
item.description: The Analects · Harmony is not sameness — Agreement and consent are different things. Nobody objected in the meeting. That is usually not agreement, and the distinction he draws says what it is instead.

item.title: Hannah Arendt · The banality of evil
item.description: Hannah Arendt · The banality of evil — Not wicked, just not thinking. What kind of state is I only follow the list and never ask why. What she saw in the courtroom changed her mind.

item.title: Hannah Arendt · Stopping to think is your own job
item.description: Hannah Arendt · Stopping to think is your own job — It cannot be outsourced. When the rules are someone else's and everyone around you complies, what is left. Why she calls thinking a duty rather than a talent.

item.title: Hannah Arendt · New York at thirty-five
item.description: Hannah Arendt · New York at thirty-five — No English, no papers, start again. New country, new language, no standing. What she had with her when she landed, what she did not, and what she did first.

item.title: The Art of Worldly Wisdom · Leave while you are winning
item.description: The Art of Worldly Wisdom · Leave while you are winning — A long run of luck is the warning. Everyone reads it as timidity. Read as written it is a gambler's arithmetic: a long winning run is the thing to distrust.

item.title: The Art of Worldly Wisdom · Do, and be seen doing
item.description: The Art of Worldly Wisdom · Do, and be seen doing — Half the work is being known to have done it. The maxim is uncomfortable coming from a priest. What it argues is not vanity but arithmetic about whose ledger your work sits on.

item.title: Atomic Habits · Fall to the Level of Your Systems
item.description: Atomic Habits · Fall to the Level of Your Systems — Goals do not separate winners from losers. Every team in the race wants to win it. What Clear says the difference actually is.

item.title: Atomic Habits · Start from Identity
item.description: Atomic Habits · Start from Identity — Do not wrestle the craving. Anything given up by willpower usually comes back. Whether there is a route that does not need the fight.

item.title: Attachment Theory · The information is in the reunion
item.description: Attachment Theory · The information is in the reunion — Not crying is not the same as not frightened. The baby who screams when the mother leaves may not be the most frightened one in the room. Which moment to watch.

item.title: Attachment Theory · A secure base
item.description: Attachment Theory · A secure base — You go far only if you can come back. Why some people will take a risk and others will not. The condition that has to be in place before nerve is available.

item.title: Augustine · Grant me chastity, but not yet
item.description: Augustine · Grant me chastity, but not yet — The oldest sentence about putting it off. Everyone quotes the prayer as a joke. Read it in place and it is an exact account of how postponement works.

item.title: Augustine · The pears
item.description: Augustine · The pears — Not for the fruit, for the theft. A man in his forties spends pages on a boyhood theft of fruit he did not even eat. The question is why.

item.title: Augustine · The mind commands itself and is resisted
item.description: Augustine · The mind commands itself and is resisted — Not a weak will, two of them. He notices something strange in the garden: the body obeys instantly and the will does not. His explanation is a mechanism, not a scolding.

item.title: Bai Gui · Take what the others drop
item.description: Bai Gui · Take what the others drop — Buy in the good year, sell in the lean one. Everyone knows buy low, sell high. What is missing is the part that makes it something a person can actually execute.

item.title: Bai Gui · Four things, and no waivers
item.description: Bai Gui · Four things, and no waivers — Missing one and the other three stop paying. He put trade on a level with statecraft and war, and then set an entrance requirement that most applicants would fail.

item.title: Jeff Bezos · Always Day 1
item.description: Jeff Bezos · Always Day 1 — What Day 2 looks like. Someone asked what Day 2 would look like. The answer, and the four parts he installed to keep it away.

item.title: Jeff Bezos · Bet on what will not change
item.description: Jeff Bezos · Bet on what will not change — The question almost nobody asks. Everyone asks him what the next ten years will change. He says the more useful question is the one he almost never gets.

item.title: The Bhagavad Gita · A right to the action, never to the fruit
item.description: The Bhagavad Gita · A right to the action, never to the fruit — Chapter two, verse forty-seven. Two thousand years of quotation have made it sound like detachment. In place it is a boundary line drawn under pressure.

item.title: The Bhagavad Gita · Standing still in front of the line
item.description: The Bhagavad Gita · Standing still in front of the line — He saw it clearly and that is why he stopped. The book opens with a man who cannot move, and spends eighteen chapters on him. That structure is the argument.

item.title: The Bhagavad Gita · Do it without gripping it
item.description: The Bhagavad Gita · Do it without gripping it — Not the same as not caring. Action without desire gets read as coldness. What it actually separates are two things that usually travel together.

item.title: Otto von Bismarck · Iron and blood
item.description: Otto von Bismarck · Iron and blood — Naming the currency a question settles in. One of the most quoted speeches in Europe was delivered in a small room. What he was arguing about there was money.

item.title: Otto von Bismarck · The art of the possible
item.description: Otto von Bismarck · The art of the possible — Three wins, then the brake. After three quick victories he spent twenty years preventing the next war. Stopping was the part that took more from him than winning.

item.title: BJ Fogg · Small Enough for Your Worst Day
item.description: BJ Fogg · Small Enough for Your Worst Day — Do not bet on motivation. On the day you decide, anything is possible. The problem is the day with nothing in the tank. What to do then.

item.title: BJ Fogg · Anchor It, Then Celebrate
item.description: BJ Fogg · Anchor It, Then Celebrate — Prompt and emotion. Forgetting to do it and doing it without it sticking are two different faults. How each one is fixed.

item.title: Murray Bowen · In the relationship and still yourself
item.description: Murray Bowen · In the relationship and still yourself — Fusion and cut-off are the same failure. With family it is either being swept along or getting out. Whether there is a third road.

item.title: Murray Bowen · Pulling in a third person
item.description: Murray Bowen · Pulling in a third person — The tension gets fixed in place. A problem between two people always seems to end up being three people's problem. What that costs.

item.title: John Boyd · The OODA loop
item.description: John Boyd · The OODA loop — Fast means turning, not moving. He was a fighter instructor who could win from any position in forty seconds. What 'fast' meant in the loop he built.

item.title: John Boyd · To be somebody, or to do something
item.description: John Boyd · To be somebody, or to do something — The fork in the road. He made colonel and never rose again. The speech he gave every young officer who wanted to follow him.

item.title: Brené Brown · Guilt is workable, shame is not
item.description: Brené Brown · Guilt is workable, shame is not — Look at what the sentence in your head is pointing at. One mistake, two sentences a few words apart. What separates them, and why the consequences run in opposite directions.

item.title: Brené Brown · The three things shame needs
item.description: Brené Brown · The three things shame needs — Secrecy, silence and judgment, and how each comes apart. Shame is not a weather system but a mechanism with conditions. Which three it needs, and how you take each one away.

item.title: Bruce Lee · Be like water
item.description: Bruce Lee · Be like water — Shape follows the container. The line is on film, so it is not something admirers put in his mouth later. What it describes is an operation.

item.title: Bruce Lee · One kick, ten thousand times
item.description: Bruce Lee · One kick, ten thousand times — Which repetition, and in which direction. A man famous for speed and variety left behind a sentence about repetition. The two are not in tension.

item.title: Warren Buffett · The circle of competence
item.description: Warren Buffett · The circle of competence — The edge matters more than the size. Everyone hears it as a licence to stay small. The working part is the sentence after it, and it is about the edge.

item.title: Warren Buffett · You find out at low tide
item.description: Warren Buffett · You find out at low tide — Risk shows up late, on purpose. In a rising market every stroke looks good. The question is how to see the risk while it is still invisible.

item.title: John Cacioppo · Loneliness is a kind of hunger
item.description: John Cacioppo · Loneliness is a kind of hunger — A signal, not a personality. What loneliness actually is. Why thirty years of research put it in the same category as hunger and thirst.

item.title: John Cacioppo · Loneliness makes you misread faces
item.description: John Cacioppo · Loneliness makes you misread faces — The more watchful, the more alone. Why loneliness feeds itself. The loop Cacioppo found, and where you can cut it.

item.title: John Cacioppo · More socialising doesn't fix it
item.description: John Cacioppo · More socialising doesn't fix it — The meta-analysis ranks it third. The most common advice for loneliness performs worst. What came first in the data.

item.title: Julius Caesar · The die is cast
item.description: Julius Caesar · The die is cast — The step that has no way back. Taking an army across that small river meant civil war. This one is about what he was calculating while he stood there.

item.title: Julius Caesar · Mercy as a weapon
item.description: Julius Caesar · Mercy as a weapon — A new way of winning. In the civil war he killed no prisoners and confiscated no property. He set out his motive plainly in a letter.

item.title: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Leave a step on the narrow path
item.description: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Leave a step on the narrow path — What you give up is your own way back. You are tight with everyone and tired either way. This asks why the book files giving way under making your own life lighter.

item.title: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Keep the skill out of sight
item.description: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Keep the skill out of sight — Not all of what you have has to be on display. Afraid of being found out, and unable to stop proving yourself. This asks what the book offers as somewhere to stand.

item.title: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Do not measure them by yourself
item.description: Tending the Roots of Wisdom · Do not measure them by yourself — Where the sourness at good news comes from. Someone close does well and something in you goes cold. This asks where the book puts the root of it.

item.title: Cal Newport · Attention Residue
item.description: Cal Newport · Attention Residue — The cost is not those few minutes. What one quick look actually costs. How the account should be worked out.

item.title: Cal Newport · Book the Block
item.description: Cal Newport · Book the Block — The gap will not appear on its own. The thing you will do when you have time never starts. How to take the time instead.

item.title: Cao Cao · Ability only, character not examined
item.description: Cao Cao · Ability only, character not examined — One test, and it is a hard one. He announced in public that he would look at ability and not at conduct. Under what conditions that extreme rule holds.

item.title: Cao Cao · Grow the grain yourself
item.description: Cao Cao · Grow the grain yourself — Fix your own supply first. The same collapse, and every warlord was seizing food. What he did instead was the thing nobody else had patience for.

item.title: Cao Cao · Burning the letters at Guandu
item.description: Cao Cao · Burning the letters at Guandu — Some accounts must not be settled. A stack of evidence in hand, enough to name everyone who hedged against you. Why he burned it in front of everybody.

item.title: Carl Rogers · Unconditional positive regard
item.description: Carl Rogers · Unconditional positive regard — Accept the person, judge the act. Unconditional sounds like having no standards. What exactly is the thing that carries no conditions.

item.title: Carl Rogers · Say it back until they nod
item.description: Carl Rogers · Say it back until they nod — Empathy is a move, not a sentence. I understand how you feel does nothing at all. What the act of empathy actually consists of.

item.title: Chris Voss · Say their feeling out loud
item.description: Chris Voss · Say their feeling out loud — Name it before you negotiate it. The other side has gone quiet and will not take a call. What Voss says to say first, and why it is not a concession.

item.title: Chris Voss · You want that's right, not yes
item.description: Chris Voss · You want that's right, not yes — Two kinds of agreement, nothing alike. They nodded and nothing moved afterwards. This is about telling which of the two agreements you actually walked out with.

item.title: Chu Shijian · Up the mountain at seventy-four
item.description: Chu Shijian · Up the mountain at seventy-four — Beginning one thing from zero. Is it too late to begin at this age? What he decided in the year he turned seventy-four, and the arithmetic behind it.

item.title: Chu Shijian · Oranges take five years
item.description: Chu Shijian · Oranges take five years — He had done the sums before planting. Everything is invested and nothing is visible for years. What he did with that stretch, and why it was not waiting.

item.title: Chu Shijian · The one thing he carried out
item.description: Chu Shijian · The one thing he carried out — Running a thing properly. Strip away the position and the title and what is left of a person. What he carried from the cigarette factory to the hillside.

item.title: Winston Churchill · The wilderness years
item.description: Winston Churchill · The wilderness years — The decade nobody called him. Shut out, nobody consulting you, and no end in sight. What Churchill did with each of those days.

item.title: Winston Churchill · Saying it and nobody listening
item.description: Winston Churchill · Saying it and nobody listening — He put it in a form you could check. You see something others haven't, you say it, nobody listens. How he said it during those years.

item.title: Winston Churchill · The year he turned sixty-five
item.description: Winston Churchill · The year he turned sixty-five — The call came a decade later. You've been accumulating a long time with no way out in sight. What the day he was waiting for actually required.

item.title: The Crowd · The person who walks into a crowd
item.description: The Crowd · The person who walks into a crowd — The steps all go downward. Why do decent people in a group do things none of them would do alone? Le Bon lays out three steps down.

item.title: The Crowd · Affirm, repeat, infect
item.description: The Crowd · Affirm, repeat, infect — The three moves that persuade a crowd. He reduced the demagogue's method to three verbs. This is why the recipe works, and what defence is left.

item.title: Crucial Conversations · Safety before content
item.description: Crucial Conversations · Safety before content — An unsafe person takes in nothing. Every sentence you say is correct and the other person keeps retreating. What has to stop at that moment.

item.title: Crucial Conversations · Start with heart
item.description: Crucial Conversations · Start with heart — Settle what you actually want. Halfway through the row you no longer remember what you set out to fix. How the goal got swapped.

item.title: C.S. Lewis · Nobody told me grief felt like fear
item.description: C.S. Lewis · Nobody told me grief felt like fear — A Grief Observed. What the feeling actually is when you've just lost someone. Why Lewis called it fear, and what that's for.

item.title: C.S. Lewis · My faith turned out to be a house of cards
item.description: C.S. Lewis · My faith turned out to be a house of cards — You find out when it's knocked down. What held you up your whole life didn't hold this time. What Lewis wrote when he found that out about himself.

item.title: C.S. Lewis · I'm afraid of replacing her with my memory of her
item.description: C.S. Lewis · I'm afraid of replacing her with my memory of her — The harder you grip, the more it warps. You're afraid time will erase them. Lewis found the opposite problem, and it frightened him more.

item.title: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi · The Channel at the Edge of Your Skill
item.description: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi · The Channel at the Edge of Your Skill — Too hard is anxiety, too easy is boredom. The same task can make you lose track of time or make you squirm. What makes the difference.

item.title: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi · The Best Moments Are Not in Your Leisure
item.description: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi · The Best Moments Are Not in Your Leisure — The data contradicted the common sense. Everyone assumes leisure is where the happiness is. Why the recorded results came out the other way.

item.title: Marie Curie · She took over his course
item.description: Marie Curie · She took over his course — Starting where he stopped. The person who mattered most is suddenly gone and the days still have to continue. What she did seven months later.

item.title: Marie Curie · A notebook written to the dead
item.description: Marie Curie · A notebook written to the dead — What you can't say aloud, write to him. There are things you cannot say to a living person. Where those go. What she put in the notebook that year.

item.title: Marie Curie · The little Curies
item.description: Marie Curie · The little Curies — Put the skill where it's needed now. Your skill and what's in front of you don't match. Where she put hers when the war started.

item.title: Ray Dalio · Pain plus reflection
item.description: Ray Dalio · Pain plus reflection — What 1982 actually cost him. He destroyed his own firm and later called it one of the best things that ever happened to him. The step in between is the point.

item.title: Ray Dalio · Weigh the opinion, do not count it
item.description: Ray Dalio · Weigh the opinion, do not count it — Neither a vote nor a verdict. He rejects the boss deciding and he rejects one person one vote. What replaces them is a weighting, and it needs a record to run on.

item.title: Peter Drucker · The purpose is to create a customer
item.description: Peter Drucker · The purpose is to create a customer — Defining the business from the outside in. Ask why a business exists and most people answer profit. Why he called that answer not merely wrong but harmful.

item.title: Peter Drucker · Doing efficiently what should not be done
item.description: Peter Drucker · Doing efficiently what should not be done — Effectiveness comes before efficiency. He pulled apart two words that get used interchangeably. Why a gain in efficiency can conceal an error of direction.

item.title: Du Fu · Ten Years in Chang'an
item.description: Du Fu · Ten Years in Chang'an — At dawn the rich man's gate, at dusk his horses' dust. What ten years of not getting there actually looks like, and what Du Fu did with the record of it.

item.title: Du Fu · I Came In and Heard Wailing
item.description: Du Fu · I Came In and Heard Wailing — He wrote the thing he least wanted to write. Something happened that you are ashamed of. Whether to say it. Why Du Fu put his son's death into a poem.

item.title: Du Fu · Forty-eight, a Hut in Chengdu
item.description: Du Fu · Forty-eight, a Hut in Chengdu — Build a roof, not a position. Is it too late to begin again in middle age. What Du Fu did first after he walked away, and what he wrote.

item.title: Duan Yongping · Do the right thing, then do the thing right
item.description: Duan Yongping · Do the right thing, then do the thing right — The two halves have an order. He has repeated one sentence for decades. Why its halves cannot be swapped, and what the stop-doing list is for.

item.title: Duan Yongping · Dare to be last
item.description: Duan Yongping · Dare to be last — Come first from behind. Everybody races to launch first; he says openly that he aims to be last. Under what conditions late is an advantage.

item.title: Carol Dweck · Praise the process, not the talent
item.description: Carol Dweck · Praise the process, not the talent — Praising cleverness makes people avoid challenge. One sentence of praise changes what a child picks next. This piece is about where the change happens.

item.title: Carol Dweck · The effect is much smaller than the popular story
item.description: Carol Dweck · The effect is much smaller than the popular story — The boundary worth drawing. The concept got told as a master key. This piece is about how big it actually is.

item.title: Albert Einstein · Changing the question
item.description: Albert Einstein · Changing the question — The answer's ceiling is set by the question. The line comes from a book he wrote, not from a quotation card. What matters is how he used it himself.

item.title: Albert Einstein · The patent office years
item.description: Albert Einstein · The patent office years — What the margin buys you. In 1905 he published four papers that changed physics. His job title was technical examiner, third class.

item.title: Epictetus · Sort it before you feel anything
item.description: Epictetus · Sort it before you feel anything — The handbook opens with a filing rule, not with advice. The one Stoic line everybody knows, put back where it starts: as the first operation, before the appraisal and before the feeling.

item.title: Epictetus · Not the thing, the view you took of it
item.description: Epictetus · Not the thing, the view you took of it — Between the event and the pain there is a step you added. Handbook five is two sentences long. The question worth asking is why it reaches for the death of Socrates as its example.

item.title: Anders Ericsson · Practising what you can already do is rest
item.description: Anders Ericsson · Practising what you can already do is rest — Stay at the edge of what you cannot do. Two people practise three hours each. One improves and one does not. This page is about what the hours contained.

item.title: Anders Ericsson · Ten thousand hours is a misreading
item.description: Anders Ericsson · Ten thousand hours is a misreading — He spent years saying so. The number travelled much further than the research it came from. This page is about what it got wrong.

item.title: Excellent Sheep · Good at hurdles, bad at choosing a road
item.description: Excellent Sheep · Good at hurdles, bad at choosing a road — Two completely different abilities. Why people who succeeded at every stage go blank the moment the standards stop. What they never practised.

item.title: Excellent Sheep · Give yourself time with no scoreboard
item.description: Excellent Sheep · Give yourself time with no scoreboard — Any standard becomes a thing to optimise. How to find out what you actually want. The condition that has to be true first.

item.title: Fan Li · In a drought, stock boats
item.description: Fan Li · In a drought, stock boats — Buy it when nobody wants it. When is a thing cheapest? At the moment everybody agrees it is useless.

item.title: Fan Li · Long neck, beak like a bird
item.description: Fan Li · Long neck, beak like a bird — Read the ending off the person. He left the moment Yue destroyed Wu, at the highest point. What he was reading when he decided.

item.title: Feng Dao · Only the emperor can save them
item.description: Feng Dao · Only the emperor can save them — If you cannot change it, change the sentence. The Khitan have destroyed the dynasty and the plain expects a massacre. What can a man with no army do in that room?

item.title: Feng Dao · The old man of everlasting joy
item.description: Feng Dao · The old man of everlasting joy — A thousand years of argument. He served four dynasties and ten emperors and named himself after contentment. The question is where his accusers and his defenders each stand.

item.title: Richard Feynman · The first person not to fool is you
item.description: Richard Feynman · The first person not to fool is you — And you are the easiest one. He put this ahead of every method in science. This page is about why the first line of defence points inward.

item.title: Richard Feynman · If you cannot teach it, you have not got it
item.description: Richard Feynman · If you cannot teach it, you have not got it — Jargon is where the hole hides. The internet sells this as a study hack in four steps. This page is about the harder claim sitting underneath it.

item.title: Finite and Infinite Games · Two kinds of games
item.description: Finite and Infinite Games · Two kinds of games — Work out which one you are in. The first sentence of the book is the whole conclusion. What the two categories save you from getting wrong.

item.title: Finite and Infinite Games · Playing with the boundaries
item.description: Finite and Infinite Games · Playing with the boundaries — Rules are props, not walls. The two kinds of player treat rules in opposite ways. What separates changing the rules from simply cheating.

item.title: Viktor Frankl · The last freedom
item.description: Viktor Frankl · The last freedom — Where the sentence was collected matters as much as the sentence. Written from a study it would be a maxim. The question worth asking is where the evidence for it was gathered.

item.title: Viktor Frankl · Happiness cannot be pursued
item.description: Viktor Frankl · Happiness cannot be pursued — Some targets disappear the moment you aim at them. The people who make happiness the goal are the ones who miss it. The mechanism he gives, and the route around it.

item.title: Benjamin Franklin · One virtue a week
item.description: Benjamin Franklin · One virtue a week — Even character has to be put on a schedule. He drew up thirteen virtues, then did the thing nobody resolving to improve ever does. The design of the little book.

item.title: Benjamin Franklin · Give up the word certainly
item.description: Benjamin Franklin · Give up the word certainly — He changed the sentence, not the opinion. Somebody told him to his face that he was insufferable. What he changed was not what he thought but how he phrased it.

item.title: Fukuzawa Yukichi · The signs in Yokohama
item.description: Fukuzawa Yukichi · The signs in Yokohama — Years of study, and not one word legible. Years of hard study turn out to be the wrong thing. What he did the day after he found out.

item.title: Fukuzawa Yukichi · Practical learning
item.description: Fukuzawa Yukichi · Practical learning — Learn what you will use tomorrow first. What to study, and whether to keep studying. What he put ahead of the Confucian classics, and the reason he gave.

item.title: Fukuzawa Yukichi · Heaven creates no man above another
item.description: Fukuzawa Yukichi · Heaven creates no man above another — The gap is in study, not in birth. You suspect you were born with less. Why the book opens on that sentence, and what its second half actually claims.

item.title: Gandhi · The salt march
item.description: Gandhi · The salt march — Pick a target nobody has to explain. How do you take on an empire, and where? This is why the smallest item on the list was the right place to start.

item.title: Gandhi · The means are the seed
item.description: Gandhi · The means are the seed — However you win is what you get. If the cause is right, can the method be rough? He closed the question in 1909 with a single image.

item.title: John Gottman · The four horsemen
item.description: John Gottman · The four horsemen — Four signals that predict a breakup. He watches fifteen minutes of one argument. This piece is about what he is actually watching.

item.title: John Gottman · Repair attempts
item.description: John Gottman · Repair attempts — Whether you fight matters less than whether you stop. Healthy relationships argue fiercely too. So where do they differ from the ones that break.

item.title: Benjamin Graham · Mr. Market
item.description: Benjamin Graham · Mr. Market — A quote is a service, not a verdict. He turns the entire market into one manic-depressive business partner. What that story actually unlocks is smaller and stranger than it looks.

item.title: Benjamin Graham · The margin of safety
item.description: Benjamin Graham · The margin of safety — The room you leave for being wrong. He said the whole secret of sound investment fits in three words. The question is what those three words are actually buying.

item.title: Mark Granovetter · The strength of weak ties
item.description: Mark Granovetter · The strength of weak ties — Opportunity arrives from people you rarely see. Who to ask when you're looking for work. Your instinct gives the wrong answer; here's what the data gave.

item.title: Mark Granovetter · No strong tie is a bridge
item.description: Mark Granovetter · No strong tie is a bridge — The people closest to you know what you know. It sounds like a turn of phrase. It's a structural result, and here is what it rests on.

item.title: Andy Grove · The revolving door test
item.description: Andy Grove · The revolving door test — Become your own successor. Intel was built on memory chips and nearly died of them. What was said in one office in 1985.

item.title: Andy Grove · Inflection points and the people who warn you
item.description: Andy Grove · Inflection points and the people who warn you — The channel bad news travels down. When the tenfold change arrives the top floor is almost always last to hear. His prescription for that structural lag.

item.title: Guan Zhong · Full granaries come before manners
item.description: Guan Zhong · Full granaries come before manners — Look at the accounts before the values. Why does saying it again never land. He inverted the order: check the storehouse first, discuss propriety second.

item.title: Guan Zhong · Government succeeds by following what people want
item.description: Guan Zhong · Government succeeds by following what people want — Dig the channel where the wanting goes. A policy that will not go through is rarely an execution problem. The single measure he used to test one.

item.title: Guan Zhong · Buying deer to break Chu
item.description: Guan Zhong · Buying deer to break Chu — Fight with prices. How do you actually make a rival yield without a single soldier. One economic campaign, run end to end, long ago.

item.title: Guiguzi · Open and close
item.description: Guiguzi · Open and close — Decide which one this is before you speak. The most important decision in a conversation gets made before it starts. This asks which of the two decisions this one is.

item.title: Guiguzi · Listening in reverse
item.description: Guiguzi · Listening in reverse — To make him talk, stop talking. How do you get a person who does not want to talk to talk? The answer is four reversals, and one precondition under them.

item.title: Guiguzi · Sounding out what he wants
item.description: Guiguzi · Sounding out what he wants — Measure at the peaks, not in the middle. What a person says day to day and what he actually wants are rarely the same. This asks when the reading comes out true.

item.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel · Yali's question
item.description: Guns, Germs, and Steel · Yali's question — Move the cause off the people. The whole book is an answer to one question asked to his face. Why the answer moved from people to place.

item.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel · The axis of a continent
item.description: Guns, Germs, and Steel · The axis of a continent — What a starting line looks like. Eurasia lies sideways; the Americas and Africa stand upright. Why a fact from school geography is worth a chapter.

item.title: Guo Jia · Ten defeats, ten victories
item.description: Guo Jia · Ten defeats, ten victories — Morale broken into checkable items. Facing an opponent stronger on every axis, how do you make a team believe? He said nothing encouraging at all.

item.title: Guo Jia · Leave the baggage, march light
item.description: Guo Jia · Leave the baggage, march light — Speed is what is left after subtraction. Everyone said a thousand-mile raid was too risky. He said the risk was not the distance but what you were carrying.

item.title: Guo Jia · The last plan: Liaodong
item.description: Guo Jia · The last plan: Liaodong — Do not press, and they turn on each other. The remnants fled onto somebody else's ground. Do you chase? The plan he left behind runs against the instinct.

item.title: Guo Ziyi · The gates were never shut
item.description: Guo Ziyi · The gates were never shut — Be visible whenever anyone looks. The usual way to survive outranking your emperor is to shrink. He did the opposite, and could explain the arithmetic.

item.title: Guo Ziyi · He rode out without armour
item.description: Guo Ziyi · He rode out without armour — Trading a battle for who you are. Hundreds of thousands of troops on the border, ten thousand men on his side. This is about why he took his helmet off.

item.title: Han Feizi · Don't build a system that needs good people
item.description: Han Feizi · Don't build a system that needs good people — Make the right move the cheap one. A system that only runs when people are conscientious hasn't started working yet. How to design rules that don't need it.

item.title: Han Feizi · The two handles
item.description: Han Feizi · The two handles — Reward and punishment can't be lent out. What power actually consists of. It turns out to be two things, and neither can be handed to anyone.

item.title: Han Feizi · Match the deed to the word
item.description: Han Feizi · Match the deed to the word — What was said, what was done. The hard part of review isn't setting standards. It's what you do when the standard and the facts disagree.

item.title: Han Xin · With the river at their backs
item.description: Han Xin · With the river at their backs — Take the retreat away first. Drawing up with a river behind you is the classic blunder, and he won anyway. Two preconditions get left out of the telling.

item.title: Han Xin · Neither revolt nor retire
item.description: Han Xin · Neither revolt nor retire — The middle is the dangerous place. He held the chance to split the empire three ways and the chance to walk away whole. Taking neither is what killed him.

item.title: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Your relationships at 50 predict your body at 80
item.description: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Your relationships at 50 predict your body at 80 — More accurate than cholesterol. What actually decides how healthy you are late in life. What eighty years of tracking put in first place.

item.title: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Relationships need training, like a body
item.description: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Relationships need training, like a body — Untrained, they decline. Everyone knows a body declines without training. So do relationships. What social fitness actually asks you to do.

item.title: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Who can you call at 2am
item.description: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Who can you call at 2am — The count doesn't matter, the catch does. The shortest way to measure your relationships. Why this question is so hard to fool.

item.title: Friedrich Hayek · Knowledge is dispersed
item.description: Friedrich Hayek · Knowledge is dispersed — Nobody can hold the whole picture. A paper of a dozen pages, later voted one of the century's most important in economics. What assumption it destroyed.

item.title: Friedrich Hayek · The fatal conceit
item.description: Friedrich Hayek · The fatal conceit — The curious task of economics. He defined his own discipline's task as pouring cold water, not forecasting. Why the cleverest people need that water most.

item.title: Arlie Hochschild · The second shift
item.description: Arlie Hochschild · The second shift — The shift that starts when work ends. Housework and care have never appeared on a timesheet. Who ends up paying when nobody counts them.

item.title: Arlie Hochschild · Emotional labour
item.description: Arlie Hochschild · Emotional labour — That smile isn't hers. Some jobs ask you not only to do the work but to feel the right thing. What that requirement costs.

item.title: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · A craft that ended in one night
item.description: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · A craft that ended in one night — 1 July 1978. What it looks like when an entire trade disappears at once. What happened to the compositors the morning after.

item.title: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · The most valuable part went first
item.description: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · The most valuable part went first — The thing they were fastest at. Why the most skilled are often replaced first. The conditions under which mastery turns into a liability.

item.title: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · Who made it across
item.description: The Last Hot-Metal Edition · Who made it across — Not the fastest hands. Why some people came through the same shock. What the ones who stayed were actually holding, rather than luck.

item.title: Hu Xueyan · The board that faces inward
item.description: Hu Xueyan · The board that faces inward — Put the rule where the cheating is possible. Adulterating medicine is easy and almost never detected. What is worth studying is where he chose to hang the rule about it.

item.title: Hu Xueyan · The silk corner
item.description: Hu Xueyan · The silk corner — What it costs to bet everything once. The richest merchant in the empire lost everything inside two years. The interesting question is which step was the mistake.

item.title: Jensen Huang · Zero-billion-dollar markets
item.description: Jensen Huang · Zero-billion-dollar markets — Entering before the market exists. He has his own name for how the company chooses. How to stay alive inside a market that does not exist yet.

item.title: Jensen Huang · Retreating with dignity
item.description: Jensen Huang · Retreating with dignity — The second story in the Taipei address. One of the three stories he told the graduates is about giving up. Why he says retreat is hardest for the ablest.

item.title: Huineng · There was never a thing there
item.description: Huineng · There was never a thing there — Subtraction is harder than addition. Two verses. Everyone admired one; the other went to an illiterate kitchen worker. What separates them.

item.title: Huineng · The practice is here, not elsewhere
item.description: Huineng · The practice is here, not elsewhere — There is no better place to start. People wait for a quiet enough setting to begin. Why Huineng said that setting doesn't exist.

item.title: Huo Qubing · Never mind the old manuals
item.description: Huo Qubing · Never mind the old manuals — Read the ground, not the book. The emperor offered to teach him the classics of war and he declined. The question is whether that was arrogance or judgement.

item.title: Huo Qubing · Feed off the enemy
item.description: Huo Qubing · Feed off the enemy — A supply line is also a leash. The hard limit on any long march is grain. This one is about how he took the limit away altogether.

item.title: The I Ching · The hidden dragon does not act
item.description: The I Ching · The hidden dragon does not act — Newly in place, do not move yet. Just arrived, just promoted, just moved. This one asks why the first line of the first hexagram says do not act.

item.title: The I Ching · The overreaching dragon repents
item.description: The I Ching · The overreaching dragon repents — The line above the peak. What the risk is when everything has gone your way for a long time, and why the top line is not the best one.

item.title: The I Ching · After Peace comes Standstill
item.description: The I Ching · After Peace comes Standstill — Run it to the limit and it turns. What to prepare when everything is going well, and what to hope for when it is jammed. Why the two sit side by side.

item.title: Ivan Illich · The two watersheds
item.description: Ivan Illich · The two watersheds — A tool that starts eating its own purpose. Everyone says tools are neutral and it depends how you use them. What is worth reading is why he says they are not.

item.title: Ivan Illich · Count what the tool costs you
item.description: Ivan Illich · Count what the tool costs you — Time saved and time spent belong on one ledger. An arithmetic problem about cars, and the reason it applies without modification to the tools on your machine.

item.title: Kazuo Inamori · The way of thinking is a multiplier
item.description: Kazuo Inamori · The way of thinking is a multiplier — And it can be negative. He reduced a life to a single multiplication. Why only one of the three factors carries a sign.

item.title: Kazuo Inamori · Pure motive, no self-interest
item.description: Kazuo Inamori · Pure motive, no self-interest — Six months of asking before he started. Before entering telecoms he interrogated himself for half a year. What that self-examination was actually guarding against.

item.title: Influence · Reciprocity
item.description: Influence · Reciprocity — The sense of owing is the lever. Of the six principles he puts this one first. Why the side that gives first is the side holding the initiative.

item.title: Influence · Social proof
item.description: Influence · Social proof — When unsure, we watch each other. Everyone hates canned laughter and everyone laughs more with it. This is about the conditions that make the principle strongest.

item.title: The Innovator's Dilemma · Beaten by good management
item.description: The Innovator's Dilemma · Beaten by good management — The textbook moves that put you out. Every generation of disk-drive leaders was killed by the next. Why the autopsy keeps reading: cause of death, good management.

item.title: The Innovator's Dilemma · Small markets cannot save big companies
item.description: The Innovator's Dilemma · Small markets cannot save big companies — A mismatch of growth needs. Big firms do not fail to see the new market; they decline it. Why the refusal is arithmetic, and the remedy he proposes.

item.title: Steve Jobs · Focus is what you say no to
item.description: Steve Jobs · Focus is what you say no to — The things you cut are the good ones. Everyone says they are focused. What makes his definition worth reading is that it points the opposite way from the instinct.

item.title: Steve Jobs · The dots only connect backwards
item.description: Steve Jobs · The dots only connect backwards — Collect first, connect later. A dropout sat in on a class with no use whatsoever. The famous line about it is usually run in the wrong direction.

item.title: John Ratey · Exercise is for the brain
item.description: John Ratey · Exercise is for the brain — You can feel the return the same day. Filing exercise under the gym leaves the cheapest medicine unused. What it's actually changing.

item.title: John Ratey · When anxious, move before you think
item.description: John Ratey · When anxious, move before you think — Start with the physiology. The more you think, the worse it gets, and knowing that doesn't stop it. Why this is the moment to go outside.

item.title: Carl Jung · You can't run the afternoon on the morning's programme
item.description: Carl Jung · You can't run the afternoon on the morning's programme — Not wrong. Expired. Something feels wrong around forty. Is it a fault? Jung said it's the hour.

item.title: Carl Jung · What you push down comes back
item.description: Carl Jung · What you push down comes back — It jumps out of other people. The kind of person you can't stand — why they can enrage you instantly. Jung said part of you is in there.

item.title: Carl Jung · Wear the mask long enough and it grows in
item.description: Carl Jung · Wear the mask long enough and it grows in — Necessary, but it has to come off. What happens after years inside a role. Jung says the mask isn't the problem — here's where the problem is.

item.title: Garry Kasparov · After losing to it, he changed the rules
item.description: Garry Kasparov · After losing to it, he changed the rules — Let people bring machines to the board. When a machine wins at your craft, what's left of it. Why Kasparov invited the computer onto his own board.

item.title: Garry Kasparov · The winner wasn't the best human or the best machine
item.description: Garry Kasparov · The winner wasn't the best human or the best machine — It was the pair with the best process. What human plus tool is actually good at. Why two amateurs won a tournament where everyone could use a computer.

item.title: Garry Kasparov · He spent years arguing the match didn't count
item.description: Garry Kasparov · He spent years arguing the match didn't count — Conceding is cheaper than appealing. What the first year after being replaced usually looks like. What he did, and what he said twenty years later.

item.title: Kevin Kelly · A thousand true fans
item.description: Kevin Kelly · A thousand true fans — Not famous, but deep enough. Creators assume fame has to come first. This asks whether that assumption is necessary at all, and what replaces it.

item.title: Kevin Kelly · Nobody in the middle
item.description: Kevin Kelly · Nobody in the middle — The money has to reach you directly. The sum carries a second condition almost everyone skips. This is what happens to the arithmetic once you skip it.

item.title: Arthur Kleinman · The Disease and the Illness
item.description: Arthur Kleinman · The Disease and the Illness — Two different things. The doctor says it is manageable and your life has caved in. Why Kleinman insists these are two separate things.

item.title: Arthur Kleinman · The Eight Questions
item.description: Arthur Kleinman · The Eight Questions — The last one asks what you are afraid of. What to ask, and what to be asked, in a consultation. Why Kleinman's list has these eight questions on it.

item.title: Arthur Kleinman · When Curing Fails, Care Does Not
item.description: Arthur Kleinman · When Curing Fails, Care Does Not — Ten years looking after his wife taught him this. Some illnesses cannot be cured. What is left to do. The answer Kleinman reached after ten years of caring for his wife.

item.title: Maria Konnikova · The con artist does not build trust
item.description: Maria Konnikova · The con artist does not build trust — He uses the need you already have. The first question after being taken in is how could I be so stupid. That question is itself the wrong one.

item.title: Maria Konnikova · A transition is the dangerous window
item.description: Maria Konnikova · A transition is the dangerous window — When the old method stops fitting. One person's judgement is roughly constant across a life, yet the losses cluster in a few stretches. This is about which ones.

item.title: Kristin Neff · Self-compassion is not self-esteem
item.description: Kristin Neff · Self-compassion is not self-esteem — One of them needs a comparison and the other does not. Self-esteem is the word this generation grew up inside. The question is why it goes missing exactly when it is needed.

item.title: Kristin Neff · Three parts, all present at once
item.description: Kristin Neff · Three parts, all present at once — Take one away and it turns into something else. Self-compassion gets summarised as be nicer to yourself. It is three components, and they have to hold at the same time.

item.title: La Rochefoucauld · Nobody complains about their judgement
item.description: La Rochefoucauld · Nobody complains about their judgement — The shape of the blind spot. One sentence draws the border of self-knowledge. This is why the first admission is easy and the second nearly impossible.

item.title: La Rochefoucauld · Hypocrisy is a tribute
item.description: La Rochefoucauld · Hypocrisy is a tribute — The disguise tells you the exchange rate. He wrote hypocrisy up as an act of homage. Inside the sneer there is a working method for reading a place.

item.title: Lee Kuan Yew · Does it work
item.description: Lee Kuan Yew · Does it work — Theory comes after the result. Theorists on both the left and the right attacked Singapore. This is about the single question he used to dismiss all of them.

item.title: Lee Kuan Yew · I would get up from my sickbed
item.description: Lee Kuan Yew · I would get up from my sickbed — Welding yourself to the outcome. A sentence spoken on the edge of handing over, and it frightened people. This is about what such a binding buys and what it poisons.

item.title: Li Bi · Take Fanyang first
item.description: Li Bi · Take Fanyang first — The base camp or the capital. In the middle of the An Lushan rebellion the emperor wanted his capitals back. This is about why Li Bi called that the worst move.

item.title: Li Bi · He would not take the office
item.description: Li Bi · He would not take the office — What refusing a post buys you. He entered the centre of government four times and went back to the mountains four times. This is about what refusing rank bought him.

item.title: Li Ka-shing · Ninety per cent of the time, thinking about failure
item.description: Li Ka-shing · Ninety per cent of the time, thinking about failure — Think about losing before winning. The richest man in Hong Kong describes his own split of attention, and it is not what you'd expect.

item.title: Li Ka-shing · Knowing where to stop
item.description: Li Ka-shing · Knowing where to stop — The two characters on his office wall. A businessman famous for expansion looks up at a scroll telling him to stop. Stopping and not daring aren't the same.

item.title: Li Shimin · Listen to all sides
item.description: Li Shimin · Listen to all sides — One source is not listening. The emperor asked what makes a ruler clear-sighted. The answer he got describes an information structure, not a virtue.

item.title: Li Shimin · Water carries the boat
item.description: Li Shimin · Water carries the boat — What holds you up can turn you over. The line has been recited for over a thousand years. Under Taizong it was a piece of daily working discipline.

item.title: Li Shimin · The argument at the start of Zhenguan
item.description: Li Shimin · The argument at the start of Zhenguan — He took the slower road. You inherit a wreck. Harsh law, or lenient rule? He picked the option everyone told him there was no time for.

item.title: Liu Bang · The three men he was not the equal of
item.description: Liu Bang · The three men he was not the equal of — Saying out loud who is better than you. At the victory banquet he asked why he had won, then answered himself. The answer is not modesty. It is an exercise of power.

item.title: Liu Bang · Three clauses, and the rest repealed
item.description: Liu Bang · Three clauses, and the rest repealed — A rule nobody can recite is not a rule. He reached the capital first and held the entire legal code of an empire. He replaced it with three sentences.

item.title: Liu Bang · Turning the sentence around
item.description: Liu Bang · Turning the sentence around — A foot under the table, and a new answer. Half the sentence is out of your mouth before you see it is wrong. What he did next looks bad, and was right every time.

item.title: Jesse Livermore · Sitting tight
item.description: Jesse Livermore · Sitting tight — Being right was never the hard part. A speculator famous for speed put the credit somewhere unexpected. The chapter explains why sitting is harder than being right.

item.title: Jesse Livermore · Hope and fear, the wrong way round
item.description: Jesse Livermore · Hope and fear, the wrong way round — The instinct points in the wrong direction. Four fortunes and several bankruptcies, distilled into one rule about two emotions pointing the wrong way.

item.title: Peter Lynch · The tenbagger at the mall
item.description: Peter Lynch · The tenbagger at the mall — Noticing is only the first step. Invest in what you know is his most quoted line and his most misused. The half that gets dropped is the work.

item.title: Peter Lynch · The organ is the stomach
item.description: Peter Lynch · The organ is the stomach — Holding is harder than choosing. His fund compounded at twenty-nine per cent for thirteen years, and most of the people in it did worse. The gap has an anatomy.

item.title: Machiavelli · Start from what is done
item.description: Machiavelli · Start from what is done — How men live, not how they ought to live. He has been abused for five hundred years over one sentence. This asks what that sentence actually claims.

item.title: Machiavelli · Feared, and not hated
item.description: Machiavelli · Feared, and not hated — Deterrence has an edge, and he names it. Loved or feared is the question everybody knows. The answer has a second half, and the second half matters more.

item.title: Machiavelli · Fortune and the half left to you
item.description: Machiavelli · Fortune and the half left to you — Half is luck; the other half has a deadline. How much is fate and how much is mine? He gives a ratio, and then says exactly when the half that is yours can be spent.

item.title: Nelson Mandela · Turning the trial into a platform
item.description: Nelson Mandela · Turning the trial into a platform — Setting your own terms inside their venue. Facing a possible death sentence, his lawyers urged a plea. This is why he read a statement from the dock instead.

item.title: Nelson Mandela · Wearing the other side's jersey
item.description: Nelson Mandela · Wearing the other side's jersey — Requisition the enemy's symbol. Black spectators had spent years cheering the opposition. This is what he accomplished on the day he put the shirt on.

item.title: Mao Zedong · On Contradiction
item.description: Mao Zedong · On Contradiction — Untie one knot at a time. Everything is urgent and all of it is yours. The question is not effort but which knot to pull first.

item.title: Mao Zedong · On Practice
item.description: Mao Zedong · On Practice — Knowing arrives through doing. You understood the idea and nothing changed. This one asks where knowledge comes from, and answers: from carrying something out.

item.title: Mao Zedong · On Protracted War
item.description: Mao Zedong · On Protracted War — Trading time for strength. The weaker side that fights at the stronger side's tempo loses. This one is about changing the shape of the war itself.

item.title: Mao Zedong · Problems of Strategy
item.description: Mao Zedong · Problems of Strategy — Fight the war your weapons allow. Someone else's victory does not transfer. This one asks what a method has to look like given your ground, your people and your weapons.

item.title: Mao Zedong · Methods of Work
item.description: Mao Zedong · Methods of Work — Put it on the table. The call was right and everyone still went their own way. This one is about getting a group to actually move on one judgement.

item.title: Marcus Aurelius · What stands in the way becomes the way
item.description: Marcus Aurelius · What stands in the way becomes the way — The line, and the mechanism under it. The most quoted line in the book, and the only one many English readers ever meet. Here is what surrounds it.

item.title: Marcus Aurelius · The view from above
item.description: Marcus Aurelius · The view from above — Pull the scale back. A year from now most of this will be gone from memory. The exercise is how to borrow that later view now.

item.title: Marcus Aurelius · The morning rehearsal
item.description: Marcus Aurelius · The morning rehearsal — Go through the people you will meet today. Book Two opens with a preparation, not a reflection. The claim is that offence you expected does about half the damage.

item.title: Howard Marks · Second-level thinking
item.description: Howard Marks · Second-level thinking — Pricing in the consensus. Two people can look at the same good company and reach opposite conclusions. Marks says the difference is which level the thinking happens on.

item.title: Howard Marks · Taking the temperature
item.description: Howard Marks · Taking the temperature — Don't forecast, locate. He refuses to forecast and still bought two generational bottoms. What replaces the forecast is a reading of where we are standing now.

item.title: Christina Maslach · Burnout has three parts. Tired is one
item.description: Christina Maslach · Burnout has three parts. Tired is one — The other two warn you earlier. Tired and burnt out are not the same thing. The three measures Maslach used to separate them.

item.title: Christina Maslach · Fix the job, not the person
item.description: Christina Maslach · Fix the job, not the person — Teaching people to relax repairs the wrong thing. What to do about burnout. The mainstream answer may have the whole thing backwards, and she says why.

item.title: Christina Maslach · Six ways to be mismatched
item.description: Christina Maslach · Six ways to be mismatched — Workload is only the first. Same hours, and one person breaks while another doesn't. The six places she found the mismatch.

item.title: Konosuke Matsushita · The tap-water philosophy
item.description: Konosuke Matsushita · The tap-water philosophy — Setting the mission at the price. He watched a stranger drink from somebody's outdoor tap and go unscolded. The company mission he wrote out of that scene.

item.title: Konosuke Matsushita · When it rains, open your umbrella
item.description: Konosuke Matsushita · When it rains, open your umbrella — Management by the obvious. Asked for the secret of management, he answered in six words. Why the almost dismissive answer is the hardest one to follow.

item.title: Mencius · The people come first
item.description: Mencius · The people come first — Where the ground under power actually is. Read for two thousand years as ancient humanism. It reads better as a technical claim about where a government's power comes from.

item.title: Mencius · Two different ways of being obeyed
item.description: Mencius · Two different ways of being obeyed — Compliance and conviction look identical. Two people are doing what you asked, and the two cases have nothing in common. This is how to tell which one you have.

item.title: Mencius · The flood-like breath
item.description: Mencius · The flood-like breath — It accumulates, and it cannot be hurried. Asked what the flood-like breath was, he said it is hard to put into words. Here is where it comes from, and how it leaks away.

item.title: Montaigne · To philosophise is to learn to die
item.description: Montaigne · To philosophise is to learn to die — After he was thrown from the horse. He tells you to think about death daily, which sounds morbid. Then he reports having very nearly done it.

item.title: Montaigne · What do I know?
item.description: Montaigne · What do I know? — Put your own weaknesses on the table first. He wrote down his cowardice, his bad memory, his dithering. Not as confession. As a position that cannot be attacked.

item.title: Montaigne · At thirty-eight he moved into the tower
item.description: Montaigne · At thirty-eight he moved into the tower — He fenced off a piece for himself. The famous retirement was not a retirement. What he actually did is smaller, repeatable, and the reason the book exists.

item.title: Maria Montessori · Change the environment before the behaviour
item.description: Maria Montessori · Change the environment before the behaviour — Out of reach is what looks like defiance. Children considered unmanageable changed when the room changed. What was it that actually changed?

item.title: Maria Montessori · Help me to do it myself
item.description: Maria Montessori · Help me to do it myself — Doing it for them saves your time. Doing it for them takes two minutes. What those two minutes bought, and what they cost.

item.title: Charlie Munger · Invert, always invert
item.description: Charlie Munger · Invert, always invert — Study the ways it dies first. He was asked how to have a good life and answered the other question instead. The swap is the whole method.

item.title: Charlie Munger · One hammer is not enough
item.description: Charlie Munger · One hammer is not enough — The danger is the skill, not the ignorance. What he warned about was not ignorance. It was being very well trained in exactly one thing.

item.title: Haruki Murakami · Stop while it is still running
item.description: Haruki Murakami · Stop while it is still running — So tomorrow has somewhere to start. Not being able to write is the normal case. What to do on the day it is flowing, and why he stops there.

item.title: Haruki Murakami · Two things besides talent
item.description: Haruki Murakami · Two things besides talent — Focus and endurance can be trained. Whether a person without talent should bother. He names two other requirements, and says both can be trained.

item.title: Haruki Murakami · Nobody asked you to do this
item.description: Haruki Murakami · Nobody asked you to do this — So the reason has to be your own. How to hold a long effort nobody required of you. The reason he found for himself, and where he keeps it.

item.title: Miyamoto Musashi · No favourite weapon
item.description: Miyamoto Musashi · No favourite weapon — Do not fall in love with a tool. A swordsman who never lost a bout wrote down a rule against loving your sword. This is about why he bothered.

item.title: Miyamoto Musashi · Perception strong, sight weak
item.description: Miyamoto Musashi · Perception strong, sight weak — Two ways of looking. He split looking into two words. This is about why watching the other man's blade means you have already lost.

item.title: Elon Musk · Boil it down to what is physically true
item.description: Elon Musk · Boil it down to what is physically true — Analogy quotes the going rate; physics gives the floor. The phrase is everywhere now. What is worth having is his own definition, and the arithmetic he did on a battery.

item.title: Elon Musk · Part price over material price
item.description: Elon Musk · Part price over material price — A number that tells you where to start. He gives every component a humiliating score. What it does is turn a way of thinking into something you can run on a spreadsheet.

item.title: Napoleon · More men where it is decided
item.description: Napoleon · More men where it is decided — Being outnumbered overall is fine. He usually fought with fewer men and was usually the stronger side at the moment of contact. This is how.

item.title: Napoleon · One step from the sublime
item.description: Napoleon · One step from the sublime — A success with no exit condition. The witticism has an origin that is not witty at all. This is about the road he was on when he said it.

item.title: Naval Ravikant · Assets that earn while you sleep
item.description: Naval Ravikant · Assets that earn while you sleep — Wealth is not money. The first line cuts one word into three. What matters is where each of the three leads.

item.title: Naval Ravikant · Productise yourself
item.description: Naval Ravikant · Productise yourself — Specific knowledge times leverage. He compresses the whole method into two words. What each of the two refers to, and why the new leverage is different in kind.

item.title: Nietzsche · What does not kill me, conditions included
item.description: Nietzsche · What does not kill me, conditions included — It is a maxim, not a law of nature. Probably the most quoted sentence he wrote, and the most misused. The question is what has to be true for it to hold.

item.title: Nietzsche · Fighting monsters, and the bill for it
item.description: Nietzsche · Fighting monsters, and the bill for it — The method you borrow grows into the person who borrows it. Two sentences, and between them a complete occupational hazard notice. The question is how the change actually happens.

item.title: Nonviolent Communication · Observation first, never evaluation
item.description: Nonviolent Communication · Observation first, never evaluation — The first sentence settles it. Most arguments are lost in the first second of speaking. This is about the exact word that loses them.

item.title: Nonviolent Communication · Underneath the blame is a need
item.description: Nonviolent Communication · Underneath the blame is a need — Hearing the half that was not said. Somebody is shouting at you. Underneath the words they are asking for something. This is how to get that half out.

item.title: Taiichi Ohno · Ask why five times
item.description: Taiichi Ohno · Ask why five times — Replacing the fuse, or fitting the strainer. The same fault keeps coming back and the review was written. What his five whys found on one stopped machine.

item.title: Taiichi Ohno · Anyone may pull the cord
item.description: Taiichi Ohno · Anyone may pull the cord — The problem surfaces where it happens. What you hand out comes back wrong every time. Why Toyota let any worker on the line halt the entire line.

item.title: Taiichi Ohno · Inventory is there to hide problems
item.description: Taiichi Ohno · Inventory is there to hide problems — Lower the water and the rocks appear. Everything obvious has been cut and the cost will not move. Why he treated stock as a cover rather than a cushion.

item.title: The Old Regime and the Revolution · The moment reform begins
item.description: The Old Regime and the Revolution · The moment reform begins — Loosening the grip is what detonates. The twenty years before the Revolution were the old order's most prosperous. The law Tocqueville drew out of that paradox.

item.title: The Old Regime and the Revolution · The centralisation that survived
item.description: The Old Regime and the Revolution · The centralisation that survived — Overturn everything, inherit the core. The Revolution claimed a clean break with the past. The unbroken line Tocqueville dug out of the provincial archives.

item.title: On War · The continuation of policy
item.description: On War · The continuation of policy — You fight in order to settle. The most famous line in the book gets read as a cynical observation. It is in fact a restraining clause.

item.title: On War · Friction
item.description: On War · Friction — Even the simplest thing is difficult. He borrowed a word from physics for the study of war. This is where friction comes from and why it can only be budgeted for.

item.title: Paul Graham · Do things that do not scale
item.description: Paul Graham · Do things that do not scale — The early work is meant to be handmade. Founders think about scale constantly. He argues for the opposite direction — and is specific about what the handmade phase actually buys.

item.title: Paul Graham · Default alive or default dead
item.description: Paul Graham · Default alive or default dead — Run this number before anything else. He asks founders one question first, and most of them cannot answer it. Why it comes before every other conversation.

item.title: Esther Perel · Security and desire want opposite things
item.description: Esther Perel · Security and desire want opposite things — Which is why the better it gets, the flatter. The steadier life gets, the less you feel, and most people assume they changed. Perel says the structure did it.

item.title: Esther Perel · Feeling nothing isn't the same as something being wrong
item.description: Esther Perel · Feeling nothing isn't the same as something being wrong — First tell a wound from an emptiness. 'We can't go on like this' can sit on top of two completely different things. Tell them apart before you act.

item.title: Esther Perel · It isn't how often. It's not being there
item.description: Esther Perel · It isn't how often. It's not being there — Present in the room, absent in attention. You live in the same place. So why does it feel like long distance? What she says to count instead.

item.title: Karl Popper · Can it be shown wrong
item.description: Karl Popper · Can it be shown wrong — A theory that explains everything explains nothing. Astrology explains events and so does physics. This page is about the line Popper drew between them.

item.title: Karl Popper · Go looking for the counter-example
item.description: Karl Popper · Go looking for the counter-example — One black swan beats a hundred white ones. No number of white swans settles the question. This page is about what you should be collecting instead.

item.title: Pu Songling · Forty years of sitting the exam
item.description: Pu Songling · Forty years of sitting the exam — Never passing, and never a turning point. There's a kind of failure with no decisive battle in it. How you get through that kind of life.

item.title: Pu Songling · The main thing failed. The side thing didn't
item.description: Pu Songling · The main thing failed. The side thing didn't — And he never knew. What he spent his life trying to do never happened. What he did on the side did. Can that be arranged?

item.title: Pu Songling · Collecting stories by the road
item.description: Pu Songling · Collecting stories by the road — Using the hours nobody wants. Forty years of a tutor's scattered hours. What he did with them, and how the material accumulated.

item.title: Rat Park · Swap the cage for a park
item.description: Rat Park · Swap the cage for a park — Same rat, different situation. The most famous addiction experiment gave a conclusion against intuition. What happens when you change the cage.

item.title: Rat Park · Back home, most of them simply stopped
item.description: Rat Park · Back home, most of them simply stopped — The hardest natural experiment there is. Is there harder evidence than rats? What the numbers on returning soldiers actually showed.

item.title: Rat Park · Take the cage apart before the willpower
item.description: Rat Park · Take the cage apart before the willpower — And where this stops being true. Once you know the situation matters, what exactly do you move? How to take the cage apart one bar at a time.

item.title: Records of the Grand Historian · No empty praise, nothing concealed
item.description: Records of the Grand Historian · No empty praise, nothing concealed — The credit and the damage in one paragraph. Six characters from a later historian, and still the standard for the form. What makes doing it so hard.

item.title: Records of the Grand Historian · I find myself in much perplexity
item.description: Records of the Grand Historian · I find myself in much perplexity — Write down what you could not work out. He admits in the first of the biographies that he cannot work it out. Why those words outrank any conclusion.

item.title: Ren Zhengfei · Huawei's winter
item.description: Ren Zhengfei · Huawei's winter — Talking bankruptcy in a record year. In the company's best year he circulated an essay about failing. The parts that turn a mood into a mechanism.

item.title: Ren Zhengfei · Let those who hear the gunfire call for artillery
item.description: Ren Zhengfei · Let those who hear the gunfire call for artillery — Turning authority toward the front. Headquarters that will not release authority leaves the front line unable to fight. The organisational inversion behind the slogan.

item.title: Sapiens · Cooperation runs on fiction
item.description: Sapiens · Cooperation runs on fiction — A company is a story too. Chimpanzees top out at a few dozen collaborators. Sapiens run to millions. Harari says the difference is something nobody can touch.

item.title: Sapiens · Wheat domesticated us
item.description: Sapiens · Wheat domesticated us — The luxury trap. The agricultural revolution multiplied people and made the average life worse. This is how a species can win while every member of it loses.

item.title: Robert Sapolsky · Built for escape, left switched on
item.description: Robert Sapolsky · Built for escape, left switched on — The problem is that it won't turn off. People and zebras run the same stress system. Why only one of them gets sick from it.

item.title: Robert Sapolsky · Uncertainty hurts more than intensity
item.description: Robert Sapolsky · Uncertainty hurts more than intensity — Predictability and control. Same pressure, and one person breaks while another doesn't. What the actual variable turns out to be.

item.title: Virginia Satir · The iceberg: layers under the act
item.description: Virginia Satir · The iceberg: layers under the act — The fight is happening on the surface. The same argument for ten years and no movement. The reason is that it is being had on the wrong layer.

item.title: Virginia Satir · Four stances under pressure
item.description: Virginia Satir · Four stances under pressure — Placate, blame, compute, distract. In a fight people turn into somebody else. This is the list of who they turn into.

item.title: Scarcity · The bandwidth tax
item.description: Scarcity · The bandwidth tax — Every shortage takes the same mind. People short of money get called short-sighted. This piece asks whether that is a character trait or a description of the situation.

item.title: Scarcity · Tunnelling
item.description: Scarcity · Tunnelling — The urgent crowds out the important. The busier you get, the less the important things get done. This piece argues that is a mechanism rather than bad planning.

item.title: Thomas Schelling · The advantage of tied hands
item.description: Thomas Schelling · The advantage of tied hands — Trade options away for credibility. Game theory says more options are better. This is about the case where Schelling proved the opposite.

item.title: Thomas Schelling · The Schelling point
item.description: Thomas Schelling · The Schelling point — Meeting without being able to talk. Two people are lost in New York and cannot call each other. This is about why most of them pick the same spot.

item.title: Seneca · Time is the one cost you cannot earn back
item.description: Seneca · Time is the one cost you cannot earn back — Price things in hours before you price them in money. The same man haggles over a small bill and gives away a whole evening without a thought. Where the arithmetic goes wrong.

item.title: Seneca · Anger has a gate, and it is the second step
item.description: Seneca · Anger has a gate, and it is the second step — You cannot stop the impression. You can withhold the assent. Anger looks like a single explosion. It is three movements, and exactly one of them is available to you.

item.title: Shang Yang · Moving the pole
item.description: Shang Yang · Moving the pole — Prove you mean it before you ask. The new code was already drafted and he went and moved a piece of timber first. This is about what the timber solved.

item.title: Shang Yang · The law does not bend for rank
item.description: Shang Yang · The law does not bend for rank — The first exception is the end of it. A year into the new code the crown prince broke it. This is about how that one hour set the strength of the system for a decade.

item.title: Shi Tiesheng · Once Born, No Longer Open to Debate
item.description: Shi Tiesheng · Once Born, No Longer Open to Debate — The Temple of Earth and I. Whether to keep asking why this happened to you. Which questions Shi Tiesheng closed during fifteen years in a park.

item.title: Shi Tiesheng · Being Ill Is the Job; Writing Is the Sideline
item.description: Shi Tiesheng · Being Ill Is the Job; Writing Is the Sideline — Put the illness in first position. How to lay out a day around a long illness. What Shi Tiesheng meant by calling illness his profession, and how to use it.

item.title: Shi Tiesheng · Death Is a Festival That Will Certainly Arrive
item.description: Shi Tiesheng · Death Is a Festival That Will Certainly Arrive — Nothing to hurry toward. For people who lie awake until dawn thinking about dying. Why Shi Tiesheng called death a festival, and what that did for him.

item.title: Sima Qian · Why he did not kill himself
item.description: Sima Qian · Why he did not kill himself — The letter to Ren An. The convention was clear and he broke it. Years later he wrote one man a letter explaining exactly why.

item.title: Sima Qian · Those books were all written at the worst time
item.description: Sima Qian · Those books were all written at the worst time — King Wen was in captivity when he expanded the Changes. One paragraph of the letter is almost entirely a list of names. What the names have in common is not talent.

item.title: Sima Qian · Staying alive takes one unfinished thing
item.description: Sima Qian · Staying alive takes one unfinished thing — To complete the words of one school. The task he set himself was absurdly large. That size is doing work, and so is the fact that he did not choose it.

item.title: Sima Yi · A thousand li in eight days
item.description: Sima Yi · A thousand li in eight days — Their schedule is built on your procedure. Your opponent has your arrival time worked out precisely. What he got wrong is not the distance but whether you keep to the rules.

item.title: Sima Yi · Waiting for the moment that will not repeat
item.description: Sima Yi · Waiting for the moment that will not repeat — Wait until they stop watching. How far do you have to take feigned weakness before it works? This is about the moment the porridge went down his chest.

item.title: Jim Simons · Slaves to the model
